blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running tax compliance at the intermediate level means turning compliance into a boring, predictable rhythm. Returns are filed on the same days each period. Documentation is collected as it arrives, not chased at the last minute. Unusual entries are documented the moment they happen, not reconstructed months later from memory.

A good compliance lead pushes back politely on pressure to cut corners. When a colleague says 'let's just post this quickly', the compliance lead says 'let's post it correctly — it takes the same time'. When a manager asks for a slightly optimistic interpretation, the compliance lead asks for the written rule it is based on.

These small moments are not exciting. But they quietly build the kind of reputation that keeps a company out of serious trouble. Good compliance is, in the end, the patient accumulation of hundreds of small correct decisions.

items.q: According to the text, how should documentation be handled?
options: Collected as it arrives, not chased at the last minute
Filed once a year in a single batch
Gathered only when an auditor requests it
items.why: "Documentation is collected as it arrives, not chased at the last minute."

items.q: When a manager asks for a slightly optimistic interpretation, what does the compliance lead do?
options: Asks for the written rule it is based on
Posts the entry and documents it later
Refuses to speak to the manager
items.why: "the compliance lead asks for the written rule it is based on."

items.q: How does the text describe good compliance overall?
options: A matter of luck and good relationships
The patient accumulation of hundreds of small correct decisions
A single dramatic decision at year-end
Something only large companies can afford
items.why: "Good compliance is, in the end, the patient accumulation of hundreds of small correct decisions."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Last-minute heroics are a sign of a well-run compliance function.
Pushing back politely is part of the job.
Documenting entries immediately is better than reconstructing them later.
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza o ritmo previsível e critica correr atrás de última hora — heroísmo de última hora não é sinal de boa gestão.

items.q: The phrase "it takes the same time" suggests that the author believes…
options: Posting something correctly is not slower than posting it quickly
Speed should always come before accuracy
items.why: Inferência: o argumento é que fazer certo não custa mais tempo — logo, cortar caminho não se justifica pela pressa.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte orientando a nova líder de compliance. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let me give you a real example, because it will happen this week. Someone from the desk will walk over and say, 'Can you just post this one quickly? We're closing the period tonight.' And there won't be any documentation attached.

Here is what I want you to say. Stay friendly — this is a colleague, not an enemy. Say, 'Happy to post it. Send me the invoice and one line on what it is, and it's done in two minutes.' You're not blocking them; you're just asking for the paper that should already exist.

If the pressure goes up — if a manager asks you to read a rule a little more generously — don't argue about opinions. Ask one simple question: 'Which written rule are we relying on here?' If there's a rule, great, we follow it. If there isn't, then we're guessing, and we don't guess with tax.

None of this is dramatic. Nobody will thank you for it today. But do it every single time, and in a year people will trust your numbers without checking. That reputation is the whole job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What example does Charlotte say will happen this week?
options: An auditor will visit the office
A colleague will resign from the desk
Someone will ask to post an entry quickly, without documentation
A return will be rejected by the tax authority
items.why: "Someone from the desk will walk over and say, 'Can you just post this one quickly?' … there won't be any documentation attached."

items.q: How does Charlotte want the new lead to respond to that request?
options: Post it now and ask for documents afterwards
Stay friendly and ask for the invoice and one line describing it
Refuse to post anything from the desk
Escalate the request to a manager immediately
items.why: "Stay friendly… Say, 'Send me the invoice and one line on what it is, and it's done in two minutes.'"

items.q: When a manager pushes for a more generous reading of a rule, what single question should the lead ask?
options: 'Which written rule are we relying on here?'
items.why: "Ask one simple question: 'Which written rule are we relying on here?'"

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "we don't guess with tax"?
options: Interpreting rules without a written basis is not acceptable in tax
Guessing is fine if the amount is small
Only managers may interpret the rules
items.why: Inferência: sem uma regra escrita como base, qualquer interpretação vira palpite — e em impostos não se trabalha por palpite.

items.q: What does Charlotte suggest is the ultimate reward of doing this every time?
options: Less work during the closing period
People trusting the numbers without checking
items.why: Inferência: "in a year people will trust your numbers without checking. That reputation is the whole job." — a recompensa é a confiança, não elogios imediatos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We filed every return on the same days, so the work settled into a steady rhythm." Here rhythm means…
items.why: Rhythm = ritmo: um padrão regular e previsível de trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I don't want to ___ people for missing invoices at the last minute; I'd rather they send them as they arrive."
items.why: To chase = cobrar / correr atrás de algo ou de alguém.

items.q: "The entry was never logged, so we had to reconstruct it from memory." To reconstruct means to…
options: put it back together after the fact
items.why: To reconstruct = reconstruir: montar de novo depois, a partir do que se lembra.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "She refused to give an ___ interpretation of the rule just to make the numbers look better."
items.why: Optimistic interpretation = interpretação otimista: uma leitura generosa demais da regra, para favorecer o resultado.

items.q: Accumulation, as used in this lesson, is best understood as…
options: the gradual build-up of many small things over time
items.why: Accumulation = acumulação: o acúmulo gradual de muitas decisões corretas pequenas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no dia a dia de compliance. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The compliance lead pushed back on the request to skip the documentation." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — de forma firme mas educada.

items.q: "Under pressure to close the period, some teams start to cut corners." To cut corners means to…
options: do something the quick, incomplete way to save time
items.why: Cut corners = cortar caminho: fazer de forma incompleta para poupar tempo ou esforço.

items.q: "They agreed the new checklist but never followed through on it." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; "never followed through" = não levaram adiante.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the year-end filing." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Filing one return on time won't move the needle, but doing it every period will." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
